cor-hd-double-descent.title: Fitting the first p of D features
cor-hd-double-descent.title_html: Fitting the first p of D features
cor-hd-double-descent.html: Let x∼ND(0,ID), 𝛃Y=x⊤β+ε with ε∼N(0,σ2) independent of x, and let n independent copies be observed. For p≤D, split 𝛃𝛃𝛃β=(β(1)⊤,β(2)⊤)⊤ into its first p and last D−p entries, write 𝛃ω2=‖β(2)‖2, fit the minimum-norm least squares estimate 𝛃β^+ (@prp-proj-min-norm) to the first p features, and predict with 𝛃(β^+⊤,0⊤)⊤. With σp2=σ2+ω2, the excess prediction risk at an independent new x0 is ω2 plus the right-hand side of @eq-hd-isotropic-risk with 𝛃β(1) in place of 𝛃β and σp2 in place of σ2.

def-hd-debiased.title: Debiased lasso
def-hd-debiased.html:
Given a lasso estimate 𝛃β^λ and Θ^, the debiased (or desparsified) lasso is 𝛃𝛃b^=β^λ+1nΘ^X⊤(Y−Xβ^λ).{#eq-hd-debiased}

Its jth entry uses only the row 𝛉θ^j. The quantity 𝛉μj=‖Σ^θ^j−ej‖∞ measures how far 𝛉θ^j is from being the jth row of an inverse of Σ^.

def-hd-irrepresentable.title: Irrepresentable and beta-min conditions
def-hd-irrepresentable.html: Let XS have full column rank. The design satisfies the irrepresentable condition for 𝛃β with margin η∈(0,1] if 𝛃maxk∉S |xk⊤XS(XS⊤XS)−1sign(βS)|≤1−η. A beta-min condition is a lower bound on βmin=minj∈S|βj|.

def-hd-re.title: Compatibility and restricted eigenvalue conditions
def-hd-re.html:
Let S⊆{1,…,p} have s≥1 elements, and let K(S)={v∈Rp: ‖vSc‖1≤3‖vS‖1}.{#eq-hd-cone}

The compatibility constant and the restricted eigenvalue of the design for S are ϕ2(S)=minv∈K(S),v≠0 sv⊤Σ^v‖vS‖12,κ2(S)=minv∈K(S),v≠0 v⊤Σ^v‖v‖2. The design satisfies the compatibility condition for S if ϕ2(S)>0, and the restricted eigenvalue condition for S if κ2(S)>0. The same definitions with a nonnegative definite matrix Σ in place of Σ^ give ϕΣ2(S) and κΣ2(S).

exm-hd-compatibility-values.title: Compatibility constants of Gaussian designs
exm-hd-compatibility-values.html:
Take p=1000 regressors, S={1,…,s}, and three random designs, with columns scaled so that ‖xj‖2=n: independent standard normal entries with n=200 (the design used in Section 28.3) and with n=400, and equicorrelated normal regressors with ρ=0.5 and n=400. The compatibility constant is a minimum of a convex quadratic over the cone. For each sign pattern of vS the problem is convex, and a duality gap certifies the computed value. The table gives ϕ2(S) and the mutual coherence μ; its rows are labelled by the common correlation ρ.

Design μ s=1 s=2 s=5 Population
ρ=0, n=200 0.350 0.328 0.146 0.0045 1
ρ=0, n=400 0.238 0.479 0.384 0.177 1
ρ=0.5, n=400 0.641 0.266 0.192 0.089 ≥0.5

The sample constants lie far below the population values, even for s=1, and fall quickly with s. At n=200 and s=5 the constant 0.0045 makes the fast-rate bound of the next section numerically useless for that design; doubling n helps a great deal. The coherence bound of @prp-hd-re-basic(d) is useless throughout: with μ=0.350, 1−16sμ is −4.60 already at s=1.

exm-hd-debiased-coverage.title: Coverage of three intervals
exm-hd-debiased-coverage.html:
Take n=200, p=400, a fixed Gaussian design with correlations 0.5|j−k|, σ=1, and β1=1, β6=0.15, β11=−1, β16=0.15, all other coefficients zero. The targets are a strong coefficient β1, a weak one β6, and β2=0, whose regressor is correlated 0.5 with x1. In each of 1000 data sets we fit the lasso with λ=σ2log⁡p/n=0.245, below 2λ0 for the reason seen in @exm-hd-lasso-bounds, and compute three 95% intervals:

  • the naive interval: least squares on the selected variables and its t interval, reported only when the target was selected;
  • the debiased interval b^j±1.96σ^ωj/n, with node-wise lasso rows (λj=0.024) and σ^2 the lasso residual sum of squares divided by n minus the number of selected variables;
  • the oracle t interval from least squares on the true support plus the target.

The results are in Figure 28.5.1. For the null coefficient β2, the lasso selected x2 in a fraction 0.069 of the data sets, and in those the naive interval covered zero only in a fraction 0.174. For the weak coefficient, selected in a fraction 0.329, the naive coverage was 0.903, and for the strong one 0.915. The debiased intervals covered β1, β6 and β2 in fractions 0.960, 0.946 and 0.940 respectively, close to the oracle’s 0.943, 0.956 and 0.958 for the same three coefficients.

On the strong coefficient the lasso’s average error is −0.210, close to −λ, and the debiased estimate’s is 0.014. The standardized estimates T1 have mean 0.14 and standard deviation 0.95 (panel (a)). Two costs remain.

The debiased intervals are wider than the oracle’s (0.393 against 0.288 for β1): part of this is the price of not knowing the support, and part is tuning. The node-wise penalty λj=0.024, a tenth of 2log⁡p/n, keeps the bound μj≤λj/τ^j2 of @lem-hd-nodewise, and so the remainder, small. But it lets the node-wise fits explain much of each column: τ^j2 (0.28, 0.25 and 0.27 for β1, β6 and β2) is well below the population value 1/(Σ−1)jj, which is 34 for j=1 and 35 otherwise, and that allows a larger ωj (@exr-hd-nodewise-bound).

The second cost is a remainder bias: 0.049 for β2 and 0.046 for the weak β6, about a third of its value. This is the term rj/n of @thm-hd-debiased, at most 𝛃𝛃μj‖β^λ−β‖1, with μj between 0.088 and 0.099 and an average lasso ℓ1 error of 0.74. At n=200 that product is not negligible.

exm-hd-double-descent.title: Two shapes of signal
exm-hd-double-descent.html:
Take n=50 observations, a pool of D=200 features, σ2=0.25 and 𝛃‖β‖2=1. Figure 28.1.1 plots the exact risk of @cor-hd-double-descent against p for two coefficient vectors, with simulated values as a check. It also shows the risk of ridge regression (@thm-shr-ridge) with the best penalty for each p.

In panel (a) all 200 coefficients are equal, so each feature left out adds to the noise. No model with p<n beats predicting zero, which has risk 1.000. The risk climbs to 12.31 at p=45, is 12.94 at p=55, and then falls. The overall minimum is at p=200: 0.834. Here the best prediction comes from interpolating with every feature.

In panel (b) the coefficients decay geometrically, and the classical picture holds: a small model with p=9 has risk 0.078, and nothing to the right of the peak comes close. At p=D the risk is 0.834 again. When all features are used, @eq-hd-isotropic-risk depends on 𝛃β only through 𝛃‖β‖.

exm-hd-irrepresentable.title: An inactive variable that looks active
exm-hd-irrepresentable.title_html: An inactive variable that looks active
exm-hd-irrepresentable.html:
Let x1,x2 be independent standard normal regressors, let x3 have correlation r with each of them, and let x4,…,x500 be independent noise variables, with Y=0.5x1+0.5x2+ε and σ=1. The population coefficients of x3 on (x1,x2) are (r,r), so a3=2r (@exr-hd-irrepresentable-example). With r=0.3 the condition holds with margin 0.4; with the moderate correlation r=0.6 it fails. Both population designs have λmin(Σ)>0, so both are benign for prediction.

Figure 28.4.1(a) shows, for each sample size, the fraction of 200 data sets (fixed design, new errors) for which some penalty on a fine grid gives exactly the right signs. When the condition holds, this rises from 0.12 at n=50 to 0.66 at n=100 and 1.000 at n=800. When it fails, it rises only slowly, from 0.03 at n=100 to 0.155 at n=800, and it can never exceed the bound 12 of @prp-hd-irrepresentable-necessary, however large n is. The sample irrepresentable quantities at n=800 are 0.66 and 1.21.

Panel (b) shows why. Along the lasso path for one data set with r=0.6 and n=800, the inactive x3 is the first variable to enter, because its inner product 𝛃x3⊤Xβ/n with the signal (the mean of the x3⊤Y/n that decides which variable enters first) is 0.62 in this sample (0.6 in the population) and exceeds that of x1 and x2 (0.5 each). It never leaves. The lasso finds x1 and x2 later, but always together with x3.

exm-hd-lasso-bounds.title: How tight are the bounds?
exm-hd-lasso-bounds.html:
Take the independent Gaussian design of @exm-hd-compatibility-values with n=200 and p=1000, five nonzero coefficients equal to ±1, σ=1 and δ=0.05. Then λ0=0.3255. In 200 simulated data sets the event T occurred in a fraction 0.990, more than the guaranteed 0.95, because the Chernoff bound and the union bound are both conservative. The cone property of @thm-hd-lasso-prediction(a) held in a fraction 1.000 of the data sets.

At the theoretical choice λ=2λ0=0.651 the average prediction error ‖XΔ‖2/n is 2.3643, against the oracle’s σ2s/n=0.025. The slow-rate bound 𝛃3λ‖β‖1 is 9.77. With the compatibility constant 0.00447 of this design, the fast-rate bound is 4269.8 (computed from the unrounded values), which is useless here. The same is true of the ℓ1 bound 2914.8, against an actual average ℓ1 error of 3.594.

Almost all of the error at λ=2λ0 is shrinkage. The lasso pulls each selected coefficient towards zero by about λ, and sλ2=2.12 is close to the observed error. Panel (a) of Figure 28.3.1 shows the whole path. The smallest average error on the path is 0.1893, at λ≈0.39λ0, well below the theoretical choice. Below that the lasso admits many false variables and the error rises again, to 0.587 at λ=0.1λ0.

Panel (b) holds n=200 and s=5 fixed and lets p grow from 100 to 5000 (the first p columns of one larger design), with λ=2λ0 for each p. The error grows from 1.818 to 2.665, a factor of 1.466, close to the ratio 1.472 of the values of log⁡(2p/δ). The error tracks the λ02 in the bounds, which is logarithmic in p. The theorem gives only upper bounds, so this agreement is an observation about the example, not a consequence of the theorem.

exm-hd-two-interpolators.title: Two interpolators
exm-hd-two-interpolators.html: Take n=4 observations on p=6 regressors, with the design of the listing below and y=(1,2,0,−1)⊤. The minimum-norm solution 𝛃β^+=X+y (@prp-mat-min-norm, @prp-proj-min-norm) has length 1.322. Adding twice a unit vector of N(X) gives a second solution of length 2.398. Both reproduce y exactly. They disagree about the coefficients: the first, for instance, is −0.002 in one and −0.059 in the other. They also disagree about predictions at a point that was not observed: at x0=1 they predict 2.131 and 2.588. The data give no reason to prefer either. The minimum-norm solution is singled out by a choice, not by the data.

exr-hd-basic-general.title: A2
exr-hd-basic-general.html: Show that for every b∈Rp a lasso estimate satisfies 𝛃𝛃𝛃𝛆𝛃𝛃12n‖X(β^λ−β)‖2≤12n‖X(b−β)‖2+1nε⊤X(β^λ−b)+λ(‖b‖1−‖β^λ‖1), and that 𝛃b=β gives @lem-hd-basic. Deduce that on T, with λ≥2λ0, 𝛃𝛃𝛃1n‖X(β^λ−β)‖2≤minb∈Rp{1n‖X(b−β)‖2+3λ‖b‖1}. This oracle inequality suits an approximately sparse 𝛃β: b can keep its large entries and drop the small ones.

exr-hd-cone-nonconvex.title: A1
exr-hd-cone-nonconvex.html: Let p=2 and S={1}. Sketch K(S) and show that it is not convex. Show that for general S it is the union of 2s convex cones, one for each sign pattern of vS. This is why the example above solves one convex problem per sign pattern.

exr-hd-cone-subspaces.title: C1
exr-hd-cone-subspaces.html: Show that every linear subspace contained in K(S) has dimension at most s, and that the bound is attained. Deduce that if dim⁡N(X)>p−s then the conditions fail for every S of size s, whereas dim⁡N(X)=p−n with n≥s is not excluded by this dimension count.

exr-hd-dantzig.title: C1
exr-hd-dantzig.html: (The Dantzig selector.) Candès and Tao (2007) proposed to estimate 𝛃β by a solution 𝛃β~ of: minimize ‖b‖1 subject to ‖X⊤(Y−Xb)‖∞/n≤λ0. On T, show that 𝛃β is feasible, that 𝛃𝛃Δ=β~−β satisfies ‖ΔSc‖1≤‖ΔS‖1, and that ‖XΔ‖2/n≤16λ02s/ϕ2(S).

exr-hd-debias-low-dim.title: A1
exr-hd-debias-low-dim.html: Suppose p<n, X has full column rank and Θ^=Σ^−1. Show that the debiased lasso @eq-hd-debiased equals the least squares estimate, whatever 𝛃β^λ is, and that μj=0 and r=0 in @thm-hd-debiased.

exr-hd-equicorrelated-irrepresentable.title: B1
exr-hd-equicorrelated-irrepresentable.html: Let Σ=(1−ρ)I+ρ11⊤ with 0≤ρ<1. Show that ΣkSΣSS−1zS=ρ(1⊤zS)/{1+(s−1)ρ} for k∉S, and conclude that the population irrepresentable condition holds for every sign pattern, with margin at least (1−ρ)/{1+(s−1)ρ}.

exr-hd-equicorrelation-re.title: B2
exr-hd-equicorrelation-re.html: For Σ=(1−ρ)I+ρ11⊤ with 0≤ρ<1 and p≥2, show that κΣ2(S)=1−ρ for every S. Is the equicorrelation structure a hard case for the restricted eigenvalue condition?

exr-hd-gd-start.title: B1
exr-hd-gd-start.html: Show directly from the update in @thm-hd-min-norm(c) that (I−P)bt=(I−P)b0 for all t. Deduce that gradient descent started at b0 returns the least squares estimate closest to b0.

exr-hd-interpolation-facts.title: A1
exr-hd-interpolation-facts.html: Let X be n×p with an intercept column and rank(X)=n<p. Show that every least squares fit has R2=1, and explain why neither the F test of @thm-glh-f-test nor the residual-based diagnostics of Chapter 20 can be used. What are the leverages hii?

exr-hd-irrepresentable-example.title: A1
exr-hd-irrepresentable-example.html: In the population version of @exm-hd-irrepresentable, with ΣSS=I2 and Σ3S=(r,r), compute 𝛃Σ3SΣSS−1sign(βS) for 𝛃βS=(0.5,0.5) and for 𝛃βS=(0.5,−0.5). For which signs does the irrepresentable condition fail?

exr-hd-iterate.title: C2
exr-hd-iterate.html:
Why one correction and not two? Write T(b)=b+Θ^X⊤(Y−Xb)/n, so that 𝛃b^=T(β^λ), and put K=Θ^Σ^−I.

  1. Show that 𝛃𝛃T(b)−β=−K(b−β)+w/n with w as in @thm-hd-debiased(a), and deduce that the k-fold iterate satisfies 𝛃𝛃𝛃𝛃n(Tk(β^λ)−β)=(−K)knΔ+∑i=0k−1(−K)iw,Δ=β^λ−β.

  2. With μ=maxkμk, show that ‖KΔ‖1≤pμ‖Δ‖1, and hence that the bound of @thm-hd-debiased(b) on the jth remainder is multiplied by pμ for each extra iteration.

  3. Show that under the conditions of @thm-hd-debiased(d) with p>n one has pμ≥nlog⁡pC−1→∞ up to the constant, so that the guarantee is lost after one extra step, however small μ is.

  4. Show that when p<n and Θ^=Σ^−1, K=0 and every iterate equals the least squares estimate, so nothing of this happens in low dimension.

exr-hd-lambda-max.title: A1
exr-hd-lambda-max.html: By @thm-shr-lasso-kkt(d), 0 is a lasso estimate iff λ≥λmax=‖X⊤Y‖∞/n (check this from @eq-hd-optimality). Show that it is then the only lasso estimate. Why does the theory above not rule out 2λ0>λmax, and what happens then?

exr-hd-lasso-interval.title: A2
exr-hd-lasso-interval.html: On the event of @thm-hd-support, with Σ^SS=I, show that the interval β^λ,j±1.96σ/n for j∈S covers βj iff 𝛆|xj⊤ε/nσ−1−nλsign(βj)/σ|≤1.96. If λ=2λ0, what happens to its coverage as p→∞?

exr-hd-mu-omega.title: C1
exr-hd-mu-omega.html:
The two quantities in @thm-hd-debiased pull against each other: μj controls the remainder and ωj the standard error, and a 𝛉θ^j that makes one small makes the other large. This exercise computes the trade-off exactly.

  1. Suppose p<n and Σ^ is invertible. Show that the only 𝛉θ with μj=0, that is with 𝛉Σ^θ=ej, gives ωj2=(Σ^−1)jj, the least squares variance factor of @exr-hd-nodewise-bound.

  2. Let p=2, Σ^=(1ρρ1) with 0<ρ<1, and j=1. Substituting 𝛉(a,b)⊤=Σ^θ, show that 𝛉𝛉θ⊤Σ^θ=(a2−2ρab+b2)/(1−ρ2) while the constraint 𝛉‖Σ^θ−e1‖∞≤μ reads |a−1|≤μ and |b|≤μ.

  3. Show that for 0<μ≤ρ/(1+ρ) the minimum is at (a,b)=(1−μ,μ), with value ω12(μ)=1−2(1+ρ)μ(1−μ)1−ρ2, so that ω12(0)=(Σ^−1)11 and ddμω12(0)=−2/(1−ρ).

  4. Read the result against @thm-hd-debiased(b) and (c), and against the tuning reported in

exr-hd-near-duplicates.title: B1
exr-hd-near-duplicates.html: Let j∈S and k∉S. Show that ϕ2(S)≤s‖xj−xk‖2/n and κ2(S)≤‖xj−xk‖2/(2n). If xj⊤xk/n=r (the cosine of the angle between the two columns, which is their sample correlation when the columns are centred), conclude that ϕ2(S)≤2s(1−r).

exr-hd-nodewise-bound.title: B2
exr-hd-nodewise-bound.html: In @lem-hd-nodewise, show that 𝛉𝛉ωj2=θ^j⊤Σ^θ^j=‖z^j‖2/(nτ^j4), and hence ωj2≤1/τ^j2. Interpret: a small τ^j2 (a column that the others explain well) means a large variance for b^j. Compare with the variance inflation factor (@def-col-vif).

exr-hd-noiseless.title: C1
exr-hd-noiseless.html: Let σ=0, so 𝛃Y=Xβ, and let XS have full column rank. Show that if maxk∉S|ak|<1, then every λ with 𝛃0<λ<βmin/‖Σ^SS−1sign(βS)‖∞ gives a unique lasso estimate with the correct signs, and that if |ak|>1 for some k∉S, then no λ>0 does.

exr-hd-null-space-property.title: C2
exr-hd-null-space-property.html: (Exact recovery by ℓ1 minimization.) Say X has the null space property for S if every nonzero v∈N(X) has ‖vSc‖1>‖vS‖1. Show that this holds iff, for every 𝛃β supported on S, 𝛃β is the unique solution of: minimize ‖b‖1 subject to 𝛃Xb=Xβ. Relate the property to @prp-hd-re-basic(b) with the constant 3 replaced by 1.

exr-hd-one-observation.title: C1
exr-hd-one-observation.html: Check @eq-hd-isotropic-risk for n=1 directly. With one observation (x,y), show that 𝛃β^+=xy/‖x‖2, and use E(1/χ2(p))=1/(p−2) for p≥3 to show that 𝛃R=‖β‖2(1−1/p)+σ2/(p−2).

exr-hd-orthonormal-lasso.title: B1
exr-hd-orthonormal-lasso.html: Let p≤n and Σ^=I. Using @thm-shr-lasso-orthonormal, the lasso estimate is β^λ,j=sign(zj)(|zj|−λ)+ with 𝛃𝛆z=X⊤Y/n=β+X⊤ε/n. On T, with λ≥2λ0, show that β^λ,j=0 for j∉S, that |β^λ,j−βj|≤λ+λ0 for j∈S, and hence ‖XΔ‖2/n≤94λ2s. Show also that if every |βj|, j∈S, exceeds λ+λ0, then ‖XΔ‖2/n≥14λ2s. So the order λ2s of @thm-hd-lasso-prediction(c) is attained.

exr-hd-proportional.title: C2
exr-hd-proportional.html: In @prp-hd-isotropic-risk let n,p→∞ with n/p→γ∈(0,1) and 𝛃‖β‖2 fixed. Show that 𝛃R→‖β‖2(1−γ)+σ2γ/(1−γ), and that this is below the risk 𝛃‖β‖2 of predicting zero iff 𝛃‖β‖2/σ2>1/(1−γ). What happens to the limit as γ→0?

exr-hd-ridge-beats-ridgeless.title: B2
exr-hd-ridge-beats-ridgeless.html: Fix X of rank r and let 𝛃𝛃m(λ)=E‖β^λ−β‖2 for the ridge estimate, with m(0) the risk of 𝛃β^+ in @thm-hd-min-norm(d). Show that 𝛃𝛃m(λ)=‖(I−P)β‖2+∑i=1r[(λdi2+λ)2(vi⊤β)2+σ2di2(di2+λ)2], and that m′(0)<0 whenever σ>0. So some ridge estimate beats the minimum-norm interpolator for every 𝛃β. Compare @thm-shr-ridge-dominates.

exr-hd-sample-splitting.title: B1
exr-hd-sample-splitting.html: (Sample splitting.) Split the observations into halves I1 and I2 chosen independently of the data. Select a set S^ of columns using only the data in I1, and suppose XI2,S^ has full column rank and |S^|<|I2|. Show that if S^⊇S, then conditionally on the data in I1, the usual t interval for βj (j∈S^) from the least squares fit of YI2 on XI2,S^ has exact coverage 1−α. What does the fit estimate when S^ misses an active variable?

exr-hd-thresholded.title: B2
exr-hd-thresholded.html: (Thresholded lasso.) Under the assumptions of @thm-hd-lasso-estimation(b), let B=3λs/κ2(S) and suppose βmin>2B. Show that {j:|β^λ,j|>B}=S, and that the signs of the retained coefficients are correct. No irrepresentable condition is needed.

exr-hd-unbiased-functions.title: A2
exr-hd-unbiased-functions.html: In the setting of @thm-hd-min-norm(d), show that a⊤X+Y is unbiased for 𝛃a⊤β for every 𝛃β iff a∈C(X⊤). Show also that for such a its variance is σ2a⊤(X⊤X)+a, and that it equals the least squares estimator 𝛃a⊤β^ of @thm-proj-invariant-functions for any least squares estimate 𝛃β^.

lem-hd-basic.title: Basic inequality
lem-hd-basic.html: Every lasso estimate satisfies 𝛆𝛃𝛃12n‖XΔ‖2≤1nε⊤XΔ+λ(‖β‖1−‖β^λ‖1).{#eq-hd-basic}

lem-hd-gaussian-max.title: Maximum of normal variables
lem-hd-gaussian-max.html:
Let W1,…,Wm be normal random variables, not necessarily independent, with mean zero and variances at most v. For every t>0, Pr(maxj≤m|Wj|>t)≤2mexp⁡(−t22v).{#eq-hd-gaussian-max}

In particular maxj|Wj|≤2vlog⁡(2m/δ) with probability at least 1−δ.

lem-hd-lasso-unique.title: Uniqueness of the lasso fit
lem-hd-lasso-unique.html:
1. All lasso estimates at a given λ have the same fitted values 𝛃Xβ^λ and the same ℓ1 norm. Hence they share the vector 𝛃z^=X⊤(Y−Xβ^λ)/(nλ) of @eq-hd-optimality.

  2. Let 𝛃β^λ be a lasso estimate with support S^. If |z^j|<1 for every j∉S^ and XS^ has full column rank, then 𝛃β^λ is the only lasso estimate.

lem-hd-nodewise.title: Node-wise lasso
lem-hd-nodewise.html:
For a fixed j, let 𝛄γ^j∈Rp−1 be a lasso estimate, with penalty λj, for the regression of xj on the other columns X−j. Put 𝛄z^j=xj−X−jγ^j and τ^j2=xj⊤z^j/n, and let 𝛉θ^j have entry 1/τ^j2 in position j and 𝛄−γ^j/τ^j2 elsewhere. Then:

  1. 𝛄τ^j2=‖z^j‖2/n+λj‖γ^j‖1≥0;

  2. if τ^j2>0, then 𝛉(Σ^θ^j)j=1 and 𝛉μj=‖Σ^θ^j−ej‖∞≤λj/τ^j2;

  3. the jth debiased estimate is 𝛃b^j=z^j⊤(Y−X−jβ^λ,−j)z^j⊤xj.{#eq-hd-debiased-fwl}

prp-hd-irrepresentable-necessary.title: Failure of the irrepresentable condition
prp-hd-irrepresentable-necessary.html: Let XS have full column rank, and suppose that for some k∉S 𝛃|ak|=|xk⊤XS(XS⊤XS)−1sign(βS)|>1. Then the probability that for some λ>0 some lasso estimate has 𝛃𝛃sign(β^λ)=sign(β) is at most 12.

prp-hd-isotropic-risk.title: Risk under isotropic regressors
prp-hd-isotropic-risk.html: Let the rows of X be independent Np(0,Ip) vectors, let 𝛃𝛆Y=Xβ+ε with 𝛆ε∼Nn(0,σ2I) independent of X, and let x0∼Np(0,Ip) be independent of both. The prediction risk 𝛃R=E(x0⊤X+Y−x0⊤β)2 is 𝛃R={σ2pn−p−1,p≤n−2,‖β‖2(1−np)+σ2np−n−1,p≥n+2.{#eq-hd-isotropic-risk}

prp-hd-re-basic.title: Basic facts
prp-hd-re-basic.html:
1. λmin(Σ^)≤κ2(S)≤ϕ2(S). If p>n, then λmin(Σ^)=0.

  2. κ2(S)>0 iff ϕ2(S)>0 iff N(X)∩K(S)={0}.

  3. (Transfer.) If Σ is symmetric and maxj,k|Σ^jk−Σjk|≤δ, then κ2(S)≥κΣ2(S)−16sδ and ϕ2(S)≥ϕΣ2(S)−16sδ.

  4. (Coherence.) If μ=maxj≠k|Σ^jk| is the mutual coherence of the scaled design, then κ2(S)≥1−16sμ and ϕ2(S)≥1−16sμ.

prp-hd-screening.title: Variable screening
prp-hd-screening.html: Suppose λ≥2λ0, the event T of @eq-hd-lambda0 occurs, κ2(S)>0, and βmin>3λs/κ2(S). Then every lasso estimate has S^⊇S.

prp-hd-sparse-identifiable.title: Identifiability of sparse vectors
prp-hd-sparse-identifiable.html: Distinct s-sparse vectors 𝛃𝛃β≠β′ always have 𝛃𝛃Xβ≠Xβ′ iff every set of 2s columns of X is linearly independent. In particular this requires 2s≤n.

thm-hd-debiased.title: Debiased lasso
thm-hd-debiased.html:
In the setting of Section 28.3, let Θ^ depend on X only, and let b^ be the debiased lasso.

  1. (Decomposition.) 𝛃n(b^−β)=w+r, where 𝛆w=Θ^X⊤ε/n∼Np(0,σ2Θ^Σ^Θ^⊤) exactly, and 𝛃𝛃r=−n(Θ^Σ^−I)(β^λ−β).

  2. (Remainder.) 𝛃𝛃|rj|≤nμj‖β^λ−β‖1. If λ≥2λ0, ϕ2(S)>0 and T occurs, then |rj|≤4nμjλs/ϕ2(S).

  3. (Variance.) If μj<1, then 𝛉𝛉ωj2=θ^j⊤Σ^θ^j≥(1−μj)2.

  4. (Asymptotic normality.) Consider a sequence of such problems with n→∞, in which p, s, X, 𝛃β and Θ^ may change with n and σ is fixed. Suppose λ=2λ0 with δ=δn→0 and log⁡(1/δn)=O(log⁡p); ϕ2(S)≥ϕ02>0; μj≤Clog⁡p/n for a constant C; slog⁡p/n→0; and σ^/σ→1 in probability. Then Tj=n(b^j−βj)σ^ωj → N(0,1)in distribution,{#eq-hd-debiased-t}

    and the interval b^j±zα/2σ^ωj/n has coverage tending to 1−α.

thm-hd-lasso-estimation.title: Estimation bounds for the lasso
thm-hd-lasso-estimation.html:
Let λ≥2λ0, and suppose T occurs. Then every lasso estimate satisfies:

  1. if ϕ2(S)>0, then 𝛃𝛃‖β^λ−β‖1≤4λsϕ2(S);

  2. if κ2(S)>0, then 𝛃𝛃‖β^λ−β‖≤3λsκ2(S).

With λ=2λ0, both hold with probability at least 1−δ, and then 𝛃𝛃‖β^λ−β‖1≤8λ0s/ϕ2(S) and 𝛃𝛃‖β^λ−β‖≤6λ0s/κ2(S).

thm-hd-lasso-prediction.title: Prediction bounds for the lasso
thm-hd-lasso-prediction.html:
Let λ≥2λ0, and suppose the event T of @eq-hd-lambda0 occurs. Then every lasso estimate satisfies:

  1. (Cone.) 1n‖XΔ‖2+λ‖ΔSc‖1≤3λ‖ΔS‖1. In particular Δ∈K(S).

  2. (Slow rate.) 𝛃1n‖XΔ‖2≤3λ‖β‖1, with no condition on X.

  3. (Fast rate.) If ϕ2(S)>0, then 1n‖XΔ‖2≤9λ2sϕ2(S).

Consequently, with λ=2λ0, with probability at least 1−δ, 𝛃𝛃𝛃1n‖X(β^λ−β)‖2≤min{6σ‖β‖12log⁡(2p/δ)n,72σ2ϕ2(S)slog⁡(2p/δ)n}.{#eq-hd-rates}

thm-hd-min-norm.title: The minimum-norm interpolator
thm-hd-min-norm.html:
Let X be n×p with rank r and singular values d1≥⋯≥dr>0, and let 𝛃β^+=X+y.

  1. (Characterization.) The least squares estimates are the vectors 𝛃β^++v with v∈N(X). Among them 𝛃β^+ is the only one in C(X⊤), and it has the smallest Euclidean norm. If r=n, then 𝛃β^+=X⊤(XX⊤)−1y and every least squares estimate interpolates: 𝛃Xβ^+=y.

  2. (Ridgeless limit.) For λ>0 let 𝛃β^λ=(X⊤X+λI)−1X⊤y be the ridge estimate. Then 𝛃𝛃𝛃‖β^λ−β^+‖≤(λ/dr2)‖β^+‖, so 𝛃𝛃β^λ→β^+ as λ↓0.

  3. (Gradient descent.) Let b0∈Rp, 0<η<2/d12 and bt+1=bt+ηX⊤(y−Xbt). Then 𝛃bt→β^++(I−P)b0. In particular, gradient descent started at b0=0 converges to 𝛃β^+.

  4. (Bias and variance.) If 𝛃E(Y)=Xβ and Cov(Y)=σ2I, then 𝛃E(X+Y)=Pβ and Cov(X+Y)=σ2∑i≤rdi−2vivi⊤. For every a∈Rp, 𝛃𝛃E(a⊤X+Y−a⊤β)2=(a⊤(I−P)β)2+σ2∑i=1r(a⊤vi)2di2,{#eq-hd-min-norm-mse}

    and 𝛃𝛃E‖X+Y−β‖2=‖(I−P)β‖2+σ2∑i≤rdi−2.

thm-hd-support.title: Sign recovery by the lasso
thm-hd-support.html:
Suppose λmin(Σ^SS)≥Cmin>0 and the irrepresentable condition holds with margin η. Let λ>0, put 𝛃g=λ‖Σ^SS−1sign(βS)‖∞, and suppose βmin>g. Consider the events 𝛆A={maxk∉S|xk⊤(I−MS)ε|n<ηλ}, 𝛆B={‖(XS⊤XS)−1XS⊤ε‖∞<βmin−g}.

  1. On A∩B the lasso estimate is unique and 𝛃𝛃sign(β^λ)=sign(β). In particular its support is exactly S.

  2. The probabilities of the complements satisfy Pr(Ac)≤2(p−s)exp⁡{−nη2λ22σ2},Pr(Bc)≤2sexp⁡{−nCmin(βmin−g)22σ2}.

  3. Consequently, if λ=ση2log⁡{4(p−s)/δ}nandβmin≥g+σ2log⁡(4s/δ)nCmin, the lasso recovers the signs of 𝛃β with probability at least 1−δ.
